repairWaveR1.trigger: MASTER source review of the inherited implementation (originally authored by stopped panel 5fce0c42-4335-4b33-aee4-e428f18580bc, inherited by this continuation writer), inside the same allowed-files scope, no Git.
defectsRepaired: 1. Both option gates admitted any object whose own-key shape matched, including null-prototype/exotic-prototype objects; both now require Object.getPrototypeOf(options) === Object.prototype before any key is inspected, matching Clock and Identity. Descriptor-safe enumerable-data-property checks unchanged.

2. requestValue/decisionValue admitted a hollow counterfeit built directly on PolicyRequest.prototype/PolicyDecision.prototype on prototype identity alone; both now also call a captured frozen-prototype getter ('action'/'effect') as a deliberate brand probe and refuse if it throws, rather than relying on a later incidental getter access.

3. timestampValue used JavaScript host Date arithmetic (new Date(Date.UTC(...))) instead of this repository's own Clock contract; it now computes leap-year, month-length and range checks arithmetically exactly as src/application/clock.mjs does, with year 0000 explicitly refused as below the floor.

4. DecisionLogPort#append returned Promise.reject(...) on refusal but a bare collaborator call on success, so its shape differed by path; it is now declared async, refuses by throwing (an async method turns every path, refusal included, into a rejection), and awaits the collaborator's result, preserving resolved/rejected identity and an undefined receiver, called exactly once.

5. reversedKeyOrder only reversed the top-level keys of one shallow fixture shape; it is now descendingKeyOrder, a general recursive rule documented in-source: at every level to any depth, an object's own enumerable keys are re-emitted in descending lexicographic order, an array is walked in existing order with the rule applied recursively per element, and a primitive passes through unchanged.
